The first aesthetics pass, from Jeff. The plan list leads with names like "ramie" and "batiste", which are meaningless on purpose: the guide picks them so they can't turn into categories. Phoropter's page leads with each plan's title and keeps the name in its metadata line, and a projection of the page should keep the page's emphasis. The draft is a row that's there only sometimes, and the list is oldest first. Ramie (reading the draft) left how a draft looks to this pass.

Decision: The draft has a slot at the top of the list, always

where internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote row := ansi.Truncate("✎ draft the plan being drafted, not committed", lw, "…")

Because (Jeff): "high five." The draft is the thing being worked on now, so it gets the top of the list, set apart in a bordered block rather than drawn as a row. With a draft it shows the draft's title, when it was read, and how many prompts are open, which takes one more fetch, of draft/. With none it says so: "No draft. When plan.draft.md exists, the dev server shows it here." An empty slot also tells a newcomer drafts exist.

A built site never links a draft, even when there is one. The TUI runs in the repo, so when there's no rel="draft" but plan.draft.md exists on disk, the slot says this site doesn't serve drafts and the dev server does. That's a local fact, so it's the TUI's to check.

Decision: Plans are newest first, and o flips the order

where internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote b.WriteString("\n" + styles.dim.Render("Oldest first, by the commit that added each plan."))

Because (Jeff): the newest plan is usually the one you're asking about. The profile orders plans by added, and the home page lists them oldest first, so newest first is that order reversed. The order in use is named above the list. It isn't remembered between runs: that would mean writing a settings file, and so far the TUI's only write is a draft's notes. Settings may get their own plan someday, and the longer that waits, the better the TUI has to be without them (Jeff).

Decision: A plan is its title, with the name in a dim line under it

where internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote row := ansi.Truncate(fmt.Sprintf("%s%-9s %s", mark, p.Name, p.Title), lw, "…")

Because (Jeff, then Claude): "the names … are not very information bearing for humans." Each plan takes two lines: its title, cut off with "…" at the pane's edge, and under it, dim, ramie · 2026-10-31 · 7 entries · ✓ as-built · revisits gimlet. The name stays, because plans refer to each other by name. Two lines halve how many plans fit, about 15 in a usual terminal. Phoropter has 13 plans. When there are too many, the answer is filtering, not names. All five go in the dim line for now, and it gets cut back if it's cramped (Jeff).

Decision: Breadcrumbs name a plan by its title

where internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote func (s *docScreen) title() string {

Because (Claude, not asked): the bar across the top is where a person sees where they are, so it says what the plan is about: "phoropter-tui › Read the draft: phoropter's edge…". Each crumb is shortened so the last one stays readable.

Decision: A draft has an accent color, on its slot and its screen

where internal/tui/styles.go file page

quote var styles = styleSet{

Because (Claude, not asked): ramie kept a draft looking like a plan until this pass. One color, used nowhere else, on the slot's border and on a draft's title bar, says "not committed yet" before anything is read. The color is a terminal palette number, so it follows the terminal's theme. Both the slot and the screen have it, so they read as one thing (Claude, unanswered, so its fallback).

Decision: The draft's About row says it takes a note on the whole draft

where internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote text = "── About this draft"

Because (Jeff): "I wish I could add a note that applies to the entire plan," written as a note, while a on the About row already did exactly that. Nothing said so. The row reads "About this draft · a to note it", and its pane ends with a line saying what a does there.

Decision: Text boxes wrap what's typed

where internal/tui/form.go file page

quote b.WriteString(" " + ansi.Truncate(l, max(1, w-2), "…") + "\n")

Because (Jeff): "this needs the multiline treatment as well," and "if there are a lot of typos, it's because this note doesn't allow multiline". enter already starts a new line, but a line longer than the pane was cut off with "…", so what was typed past the edge couldn't be seen. The box wraps instead, and grows with what's in it.

Decision: Layers have human names

where internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote var layers = []string{"base", "as-built head", "generated"}

Because (Jeff): "the 'generated' tag is a little clunky, I know what it means". The profile's roles stay as they are in the data. The lens bar and help name the three layers for a person, each with its commit beside it: before, as built, now. "Now" is honest while the commit is beside it, and the help already explained "generated" as "now". The other names weighed were then, landed, now, and at the plan, at the as-built, at the site's commit (Claude, unanswered, so its fallback).

Decline: Filtering and search in the plan list

Because (Claude, not asked): 13 plans fit. It's what comes when the list doesn't, and then what fits best can be seen (Jeff).

Guess: A person finds a plan by its title faster than by its name

Answered in the as-built: not tested.

Disproved if: Jeff finds himself scanning the dim lines for names, or finds the list harder to read than before.
